# TV stickman — Style Prompt

> A calm "why does this happen?" explainer on a near-black broadcast field: refined white and grey silhouettes with blank round heads and thick rounded limbs, a cat or object drawn as soft white shapes with its own face, a thin floor line, lots of empty dark space. Compact uppercase titles state the question, a small header carries topic, progress squares and a mono counter, and the picture builds ideas with dotted connectors, label pills, red strikes and a framed CCTV insert, finished with faint scanlines, a vignette and a brief signal blip when the idea changes.

## 1. Essence, and what it is not

A **reasoned mini-documentary in silhouettes**: one question, answered in four or five beats by building relationships between two subjects (a person and a pet, a buyer and a shelf, a student and a phone). The anchor (the figure, the floor, the subject) stays put while one thing changes per beat: a connector draws, a pose changes, an object falls, a label appears, a warning is struck out. It suits everyday psychology, pet behaviour, habits, how-it-works for a shop or clinic, and short eerie-but-gentle stories.

Not a horror film (red and signal blips are punctuation, not mood), not a cartoon (faces are blank on people, no costumes, no outlines), not glossy motion graphics (flat fills, no gradients except the vignette), not a slideshow (every beat changes the picture, not just the title).

## 2. Materials & rendering

- **Field**: a flat near-black ground with one thin floor line (3 px, ink mixed ~16 % into the ground) across the middle third; no room unless a beat needs one.
- **People**: a filled round head (no face, no nose or ears; orientation comes from the body), a short thick torso (stroke ~38 px with round caps), arms ~18 px and legs ~20 px as two-segment strokes with round joints. Front limbs in `--teks`, back limbs in `--abu` so the overlap reads. About 5.5 heads tall. Never stick-thin lines, never knee crossbars.
- **Animals and objects**: soft white rounded shapes with grey patches (`--abu`) and a dark face (eyes, a nose), tables and shelves as dark grey slabs (`--abu-tua`), small props in white.
- **Label pills**: rounded rectangles in `--utama` with uppercase `--teks-di-utama` text, 30 px.
- **Dotted connector**: round 6 px dots every 18 px in `--utama-di-latar`, drawn from one subject to the other.
- **CCTV insert**: a framed rectangle (3 px grey frame) on `--latar-2`, a mono camera label top-left, a red REC dot and a running timecode top-right, the scene re-drawn small inside.
- **Finish**: horizontal scanlines (2 px of 22 % ground every 4 px) and an elliptical vignette over everything, drawn once; a bright band sweeping down plus a 0.15 s horizontal shove for a signal blip.

## 3. Colour logic

- `--latar` is the broadcast black; `--latar-2` the insert's room. A light brand flips the film to dark silhouettes on a light field, which still works.
- `--teks` draws people, animals, props and titles; `--abu` (ink mixed 62 % into the ground) is the back limbs and patches; `--abu-tua` (30 %) the furniture; `--teks-redup` the header and secondary lines.
- `--utama` fills the label pills and the CTA button; `--utama-di-latar` colours the dotted connectors. `--aksen` is a single small prop (a toy, a lamp's light).
- Fixed: `--peringatan` (a warning red) only for strikes and the REC dot.
- Rule: the frame is ~85 % ground; colour appears only in labels, one connector, one strike.

## 4. Type

- `--font-judul` carries the title: a heavy grotesk in uppercase (Inter 800 by default; Archivo Black or Oswald 700 suit), 72 px at 1080 high (84 px vertical), centred in the upper third, 2–4 words, ideally a question.
- The header in `--font-isi` 600, 22 px uppercase tracked 2 px, `--teks-redup`: "TOPIC / SUBTOPIC" left, progress squares centre, a mono "01 / 05" right (IBM Plex Mono).
- Captions in `--font-isi` 800 uppercase, 40 px (44 px vertical), one line in the lower band, often the full question or the answer.
- Labels 30 px uppercase 800. Readouts (timecodes, counters) mono.

## 5. Motion quality

- **Shot length**: 2.4–3.6 s, one beat per shot; hard cuts between ideas, each new idea may open with a signal blip (0.15–0.22 s).
- **Building inside a shot**: title fades up 16 px in 0.3 s, then one change at a time, 0.3–0.8 s apart: a connector draws in 0.8 s `power2.out`, a label pops in 0.25–0.3 s `back.out(2)`, a strike draws in 0.3 s.
- **Poses**: pose-to-pose in 0.3–0.4 s (`power2.inOut`; a reaction `back.out(1.6–2)`). Walk cycles at 0.35 s per step with `sine.inOut`. People hold still between changes.
- **Animals**: a tail sways 0.45 s per half (`sine.inOut`), a paw taps out and back in 0.25 s, the head turns.
- **Objects**: things fall with `power2.in` in 0.4–0.45 s and rotate as they go.
- **Camera**: locked, with at most a linear 1.03 push over a hook.

## 6. Camera grammar

| Move | What it expresses | Can serve |
|---|---|---|
| Locked wide on the floor line | the situation, both subjects | a pet and its owner; a buyer and a shelf; a student and a desk |
| Dotted connector between subjects | a relationship, a cause | attention seeking; a habit loop; who influences whom |
| Framed CCTV insert | observed evidence | "watch what happens"; a timeline; a test |
| Red strike over a label | the wrong answer | scolding; a myth; a bad habit |
| Signal blip on a cut | the idea changes | a reveal; a twist; a new chapter |
| Settled hold with header full | the conclusion | the answer; the name and contact |

## 7. Native moves

- **The question hook.** An uppercase question over a still scene where one object changes state. *Fits content like:* a cup pushed off a table by a cat; a light that flickers in an empty room; a shopping cart left half full; a phone lighting up during study time.
- **The connector build.** A dotted line draws from one subject to another and a label pill names the link. *Fits content like:* "LIHAT AKU" from cat to owner; "LAPAR" from a child to a fridge; "NOTIFIKASI" from a phone to a student; "ULASAN" from a buyer to a shop.
- **The CCTV insert.** A framed feed with a camera label, a blinking REC dot and a running timecode; the subject acts only after another enters. *Fits content like:* a cat waiting for its owner; a customer's path in a shop; a toddler's bedtime routine; a story's mysterious visitor.
- **The struck warning.** A pose and a speech label, a red strike through the label, then the better way appears with its own label. *Fits content like:* "HEI!" struck, then "AJAK MAIN"; "DISKON TERUS" struck, then "LAYANAN CEPAT"; "BEGADANG" struck, then "TIDUR JAM 10".
- **The calm sign-off.** Name in big uppercase, a muted line, a filled pill, the two subjects side by side on the floor line, the header complete. *Fits content like:* a vet clinic's chat; a creator's "follow for part 2"; a class link; "Tamat".

## 8. Pitfalls

- Faces, noses or ears on the people: they stay blank; animals keep their own faces.
- Thin stick lines or knee crossbars: limbs are thick round strokes with grey back limbs.
- A busy room in every shot: keep the empty field and the floor line; add a room only inside an insert.
- Red, CCTV and glitches everywhere: one strike, one insert, one blip per idea change at most; never over the captions.
- Repeating the same wide shot with a new title: each beat must change a relationship, a pose, a state or the framing.
- Heavy noise, chromatic split or animated blur for the TV finish: the scanlines and vignette are static; blips are a short shove and a band.

# TV stickman: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.4, medium 3, long 3.6.

## hook

- en: the question as an uppercase title over a still silhouette scene; one object changes state (falls, opens, lights up)
- id: pertanyaan jadi judul huruf balok di atas adegan siluet; satu benda berubah keadaan (jatuh, terbuka, menyala)

## problem

- en: the figure's pose changes and a speech label appears over it, then a red strike draws through the label
- id: pose orang berubah dan label ucapan muncul di atasnya, lalu coretan merah tergambar menembus label itu

## fact

- en: a relationship build: a dotted connector draws between two subjects and a label pill names the link
- id: membangun hubungan: garis titik-titik tergambar di antara dua subjek, label menamai hubungannya

## step

- en: the same anchor stays; one prop or pose changes per beat, a short label for each, a signal blip between ideas
- id: jangkar tetap; satu benda atau pose berubah tiap ketukan, satu label pendek, sinyal tersendat di antara ide

## compare

- en: the wrong way gets a red strike, then the better way appears beside it with its own label
- id: cara yang salah dicoret merah, lalu cara yang lebih baik muncul di sampingnya dengan labelnya sendiri

## number

- en: a framed monitor insert with a mono readout that counts, the subject small inside it
- id: sisipan monitor berbingkai dengan angka huruf mono yang berjalan, subjek kecil di dalamnya

## proof

- en: a CCTV insert: camera label, REC dot, running timecode; the subject acts inside the feed
- id: sisipan CCTV: label kamera, titik REC, kode waktu berjalan; subjek beraksi di dalam rekaman

## offer

- en: the anchor scene settles, a label pill with the offer slides in above it, a brief signal blip
- id: adegan jangkar tenang, label penawaran meluncur di atasnya, sinyal tersendat sebentar

## cta

- en: name in big uppercase, a muted contact line, a filled pill; the figure waves on the floor line; held 2 s
- id: nama huruf balok besar, kontak redup, tombol berisi warna; orang melambai di garis lantai; diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: the two subjects side by side, calm, the closing question answered in one uppercase line; held 2 s
- id: dua subjek berdampingan dengan tenang, pertanyaan pembuka dijawab satu baris huruf balok; diam 2 detik
